1. Vide the present appeal, the appellant has challenged the judgment dated 30.06.2023 (hereinafter referred to as "the impugned judgment") vide which appellant was convicted for the offence under Section 323/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as the "IPC") and sentence order dated 14.09.2023 (hereinafter referred to as "the impugned sentence order") vide which Ld.Trial Court had admonished the appellant under Section 323/34 IPC.
However, appellant was directed to Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 1/17 pay the cost incurred by the prosecution of Rs.6,000/-.

The brief facts which are relevant for deciding the present appeal are that on 29.01.2020, an information was received at PS Sangam Vihar regarding quarrel and one person getting hurt, which was reduced into General Diary No. 39A and the said GD No. 39A was assigned to HC Ravinder for necessary action.

Thereafter, HC Ravinder accompanied with Constable Jai Narayan, had reached the place of incident where they found some persons in injured condition, who were sent to the hospital for their treatment.
The result on the MLC was kept pending by the doctor.

Thereafter, on 30.01.2020, a complaint was given to the SHO, PS Sangam Vihar by the complainant Sh.
Rambhawan Ojha wherein he had alleged that on 29.01.2020 at around 6.00 p.m. near 18A Gurudwara, appellant alongwith other co-accused persons namely Rajvinder Singh @ Resham Baba,
Ravi Yadav and Surjit Singh @ Dr.Sidhu alongwith their party workers misbehaved with the National Secretary of Manavadhikar National Party and candidate of Sangam Vihar Vidhan Sabha Dinesh Mohaniya vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134787775/
1 and also made attack upon complainant Sh.Rambhawan Ojha and his brother Sh.Shivbhawan Ojha with sticks and bricks on their heads and also misbehaved with other lady party workers namely,
Neeru Sharma, Kiran Gupta, Neelam Gupta and Pooja.

It was alleged in the complaint by complainant Sh.Rambhawan that appellant alongwith other co-accused persons were involved in indecent behaviour with the lady party workers Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. his mobile phone of Vivo company was snatched by co- accused Rajvinder Singh @ Resham Baba and was handed over to appellant.

3. Based upon the complaint of complainant Sh.Rambhawan Ojha, FIR No. 41/2020 PS Sangam Vihar was registered for the offence under Section 323/341/354/354(B)/379/356/34 IPC against Ravinder Singh @Resham Baba, Dinesh Mohniya (appellant), Ravi Yadav and Surjeet Singh @

5.

During investigation, no allegations of theft/snatching could be disclosed and the complainant himself stated that he had received his mobile phone on the same day and there was no intention to snatch/steal his mobile phone.

Thereafter, Section 379/356 IPC were removed and the charge sheet was filed against the appellant and co-accused Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 3/17 persons for the remaining offences.

sentences.text: However, they were acquitted for the remaining offences.
Thereafter, appellant and co-accused Ravi Yadav and Surjeet Singh @ Dr.Sidhu were sentenced vide impugned sentence order.
10.Aggrieved by the impugned judgment and impugned sentence order, appellant has approached this court.
11.Notice of the appeal was issued to Ld.Addl.PP for respondent/State.

After being served, Ld.
Addl.PP for state had objected to the maintainability of the present appeal in the light of bar contained U/s 376 Cr.P.C and submitted that the present appeal is not maintainable since the punishment imposed was of less then three months period.

Thereafter appellant had made statement before this court whereby he prayed that the appeal be treated as Revision U/s 397 Cr.P.C, which was allowed by this court and hence the present appeal was converted into a Revision petition.
12.I have heard Sh.Manish Rawat, Ld. Addl.PP for State and Sh.Sudhir, Ld counsel for revisionist.

13.It was submitted by Ld. Counsel for revisionist that the impugned judgment is contrary to the law and facts of the present case as Ld. Trial court did not appreciate the evidence which had come on record in the right perspective.

It was further submitted that there was no evidence on record which pointed towards the guilt of the revisionist and therefore, Ld. Trial Court wrongly convicted the revisionist U/s 323/34IPC.
14.It

was further submitted that the present case was got registered by Sh. Rambhawan Ojha, who is the Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 5/17 complainant and is eye witness to the alleged incident.

sentences.text: However, in his cross-examination, PW-1 Rambhawan Ojha denied being present at the place of incident and also denied seeing any of the accused persons including the revisionist at the time of incident.
PW-1 Rambhawan Ojha also denied the complaint Ex PW-1/A being in his own handwriting.

However, Ld. Trial court still believed the testimony of PW-1 and relied upon the evidence of PW-1 to convict the revisionist U/s 323/34 IPC even though he was not present at the spot and was not an eye witness to the incident.
15.It was further submitted that PW-2 Shivbhawan Ojha was brother of the complainant and he also failed to identify any of the assailants.

16.It was further submitted that other four eye witnesses were PW-3 Ms. Pooja, PW-4 Ms. Kiran Gupta, PW-5 Smt Neeru Sharma and PW-6 Smt. Neelam Devi and they have also not deposed regarding the revisionist assaulting the injured i.e. PW-2 Shivbhawan Ojha and had resiled from their previous statements given U/s 161 Cr.P.C to the police and statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C made Dinesh Mohaniya vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134787775/
3 before the Ld. Magistrate.

17.It was further submitted that PW-3 Ms. Pooja in her previous statement recorded U/s 161 Cr.P.C,
Ex PW-3/A had stated about her brother getting injured in this incident due to which he had to be given six stitches on his head.

However, brother of PW-3 Ms. Pooja was not examined in this case nor any MLC of his was proved on record to lend Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 6/17 credence to the version of PW-3 Ms. Pooja or of the injured witnesses.

entities.text: Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 6/17
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. It was further submitted that in her statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C, PW-4 Ms Kiran Gupta had made a reference of making video of the incident but no such video was produced on record.

Therefore,
withholding of the evidence in the form of video footage and the testimony of brother of PW-3 makes the prosecution case totally unreliable and untrustworthy and ld.
Trial court had committed grave illegality by convicting the revisionist based on unreliable and untrustworthy evidence.
19.It was further submitted that revisionist was two times MLA of Sangam Vihar assembly and at the time of incident, he was participating in the election for the position of MLA.

The complainant,
who was also participating in the election, with the malafide motive just to defame the revisionist in the eyes of the public at the election time got the false case registered against the revisionist to have him arrested before the election.
Therefore, the present case is politically motivated and there is no evidence on record to prove the guilt of the revisionist.

It was further submitted that as per the evidence of PW-1, it was accused Surjeet Singh @ Dr. Sidhu, who was instrumental in causing injuries on the person of PW-2 with the help of danda and revisionist had no role to play in the said fight.
Therefore, mere presence of the revisionist at the spot is not a crime.

20. It was further submitted that trial court had committed Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 7/17 grave illegality by relying upon the testimony of witnesses, who were unreliable, untrustworthy and inconsistent to convict the revisionist U/s 323/34 IPC.

Accordingly,
prayer was made to allow the revision petition and to set aside the impugned judgment and impugned sentence order.

In support of his submission, he has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India delivered in Crl appeal no. 1750 of 2023 (Date of decision 19.07.2023) titled as Boini Mahipal and ors Vs. The State of Telangana.

sentences.text: 21.On the other hand, Ld. Addl.PP for respondent/state has submitted that there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment and impugned sentence order passed by the Ld. Trial court.
It was further submitted that Ld. Trial court has rightly relied upon the testimony of prosecution witnesses i.e. PW-1 to PW-6 despite some of them turning hostile, to convict the revisionist,

It was further submitted that the testimony of prosecution witnesses was corroborated by the medical examination report of the injured witnesses which corroborated their version regarding incident and injuries suffered by them.
Accordingly, prayer was made to dismiss the revision petition.
22.I have considered the rival submissions as well as written submissions filed by the revisionist and have carefully perused the summoned trial court record.

sentences.text: The Ld. Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 8/17 Trial court has based its findings of conviction upon the testimony of prosecution witnesses i.e. PW-1 to PW-6.

entities.text: Ld. Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW-1 Sh. Rambhawan Ojha, who is the complainant in this case was contesting the Delhi Vidhan Sabha election, 2020 and was campaigning with his party workers on the date of incident.

He had deposed on oath that during campaigning, an altercation had taken place between them and the accused persons and during the course of arguments, Dr. Sidhu had struck on the head of PW-2 Sh.
Shivbhawan Ojha, his brother with danda and also attacked some other party workers.
An altercation had started on the issue of accused persons asking the complainant not to campaign in their area.
He further deposed that revisionist was also accompanying the accused persons when his brother was attacked.
PW-1 had correctly identified the revisionist and the accused persons in the court.
24.PW-1 Sh. Rambhawan Ojha was examined-in-chief on 12.01.2023 but was cross-examined by the accused persons on 16.03.2023, that is after around two months of his examination-in-chief.

It was on 16.03.2023 when PW-1 Sh. Rambhawan Ojha was cross-examined that he failed to identify the revisionist and other accused persons being present at the place of incident and he also denied himself being present at the place of the incident.

However, since he was resiling from his examination-in-chief, therefore, he was allowed to be cross-examined by Ld. Addl.PP for State and in the said cross-examination, PW-1 Rambhawan Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 9/17 Ojha had admitted that his brother had sustained injuries on his head and he had signed his examination-in-chief after having understood its contents in Hindi on 12.01.2023.

entities.text: Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Although, it is true that PW-1 Sh. Rambhawan Ojha has denied about his presence and the presence of the revisionist and other accused persons being involved in the incident in his cross-examination recorded on 16.03.2023, but in the opinion of this court, this deposition made by PW-1 Sh.
Rambhawan Ojha was a clear attempt made by PW-1 Rambhawan Ojha to wriggle out of his deposition made in examination-in-chief, wherein he had specifically named revisionist and other accused persons, who were instrumental in assaulting his brother PW-2 Shivbhawan Ojha and for causing injuries on his head.

Since examination-in-chief of PW-1 had taken place on 12.01.2023 and his cross-examination had taken place after two months' gap on 16.03.2023, therefore during this period, the possibility of PW-1 being won over by the accused persons including revisionist can not be ruled out.

Further PW-1 Sh. Rambhawan Ojha in his examination-in- chief had categorically admitted regarding giving of complaint to the police, Ex PW-1/A bearing his signature at point A but he disowned his handwriting on the complaint Ex PW-1/A in his cross-examination.

In the opinion of this court, PW-1 Rambhawan Ojha had disowned the police complaint, Ex PW-1/A and wrongly shifted the onus of giving the police complaint by his party workers for the reasons of his being won over by the Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 10/17 revisionist and the other accused persons after recording of his examination-in-chief on 12.01.2023.
25.PW-1 Sh. Rambhawan was campaigning during the Delhi Vidhan Sabha Election, 2020 when the incident had taken place.

entities.text: Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, presence of PW-1 Sh. Rambhawan at the spot is quite natural and believable.
Further injuries sustained by PW-2, brother of complainant on his head are duly corroborated by the MLC Ex.A-5.

Further, the incident of quarrel during the campaigning between the party workers of PW-1 and the other party, whose symbol was broom, has been further Dinesh Mohaniya vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134787775/
5 corroborated by evidence of PW-3 to PW-6, who were female party workers of PW-1 and were accompanying him in election campaigning.

entities.text: Dinesh Mohaniya vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, evidence of PW-1 regarding the time, place and the manner of the incident as well as the identity of assailants including revisionist is acceptable and trustworthy, notwithstanding his failure to identify the assailants or his denial about being present at the spot in his cross-examination.

I am fortified in my reasoning by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, delivered in case Khujji @ Surendra Tiwari Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh AIR 1991 1853, wherein also the Hon'ble Supreme Court has relied upon the testimony of eye witness i.e. PW-1, who had supported the prosecution case in his examination-in-chief, but in the cross-examination recorded after one month of his examination-in-chief, he had failed to identify the assailants.

entities.text: Khujji @ Surendra Tiwari Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh AIR 1991 1853
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India had found Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 11/17 the testimony of eye-witness PW-1 to be reliable, cogent and acceptable notwithstanding the fact that in his cross- examination, he had failed to identify the appellant.

entities.text: Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, Ld. Trial court had rightly relied upon the testimony of PW-1 to hold revisionist guilty for the offence U/s 323/34 IPC as revisionist was specifically named by PW-1, in his examination-in-chief as member of the group, who had assaulted PW-2, pursuant to common intention.
26.The

other witness, which was relied upon by the Trial Court was injured i.e. PW-2 Sh.
Shivbhawan Ojha.

PW-2 had corroborated the testimony of complainant by deposing that during the course of campaigning for Delhi Vidhan Sabha Election, they were attacked by the revisionist and the other accused persons as they did not like them to be campaigning in their area and during the course of assault, he had suffered injuries on his head.

The injuries on the person of PW 2 Sh.
Shivbhawan Ojha is further corroborated by his MLC, Ex A-5.
27.
Although PW-2 Sh. Shivbhawan Ojha had failed to identify the revisionist as one of the assailants in the court but in the opinion of this court, this is of no consequence as PW-2 Sh.
Shivbhawan Ojha had specifically named the revisionist as one of the assailants in his examination-in- chief.
Therefore the identity of the revisionist was established beyond doubt.

Since PW-2 Sh. Shivbhawan Ojha was injured himself, therefore, his testimony has got greater evidentiary value and it can not be believed that the injured witness would allow real culprit to escape and Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 12/17 would falsely implicate the accused persons.

entities.text: Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The presence of injured/eye witness at the time and place of occurrence can not be doubted unless there are material contradictions in his deposition.

The aforementioned legal principles to appreciate the testimony of injured witness has been reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the matter of Balu Sudam Khalde Vs. The State of Maharashtra in Crl Appeal no.1910 of 2010 decided on 29.03.2023.
28.

entities.text: Balu Sudam Khalde Vs. The State of Maharashtra in Crl Appeal no.1910 of 2010
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, nothing was brought out in the cross- examination of PW-2 to show that the testimony of PW -2 is not reliable or trustworthy.

On the contrary, the testimony of PW-2, that an altercation taken place during the course of election campaigning between the party workers and his brother PW-1 and the opposite party of the revisionist in the Sangam Vihar area is duly corroborated by other persons of the campaigning party i.e. PW-3 to PW-6.

The name of the assailants mentioned by PW-2 in his examination-in-chief have been duly corroborated by another eye witness i.e. PW-1 Rambhawan Ojha, who is brother of PW-2 and was the contesting candidate in Delhi Vidhan Sabha Dinesh Mohaniya vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134787775/
6 Election, 2020.

entities.text: Delhi Vidhan Sabha Dinesh Mohaniya vs State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, there is no reason to doubt the testimony of PW-2 Shivbhawan Ojha regarding the time and place of the incident and the identity of the assailants and Ld.
Trial court had rightly relied upon the testimony of PW-2 which was duly corroborated by PW-3 to PW-6 to convict revisionist.

29. The Ld trial court had rightly relied upon the testimony of Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 13/17 PW-3 to PW-6 regarding the quarrel which had taken place during the course of election campaigning to corroborate the testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 even though PW-3 to PW-6 were declared by the prosecution to be hostile and even were cross-examined by the prosecution.

entities.text: Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ld. trial court had rightly relied upon the settled law that the testimony of witnesses, who have turned hostile and were cross-examined by prosecution can not be rejected in toto and the same is admissible to the extent their version is found to be corroborated by other reliable evidence.

In the present case, Ld.Trial Court had only relied upon the version of PW-3 to PW-6 regarding the fight which took place during the course of election campaigning which was duly corroborated by the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and I do not find any illegality in the same.

30.The contention of Ld. Counsel for revisionist that non- production of video recording mentioned in the statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C of PW-4 Kiran Gupta and non-examination of brother of PW 3 Pooja, who had sustained injuries during the course of fight on his head as mentioned in her statement recorded U/s 161 Cr.P.C., makes the prosecution case doubtful, deserves to be rejected.

The reason for the same is that the statement of witnesses recorded U/s 161 Cr.P.C is in the nature of previous statement and they can only be used for the purpose of contradiction as per Section 162 Cr.P.C.

In the present case, during the evidence of PW-3 Pooja, the said witness was never confronted with her previous statement recorded U/s 161 Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 14/17 Cr.P.C with regard to her brother suffering injuries on his head during the course of fight.

entities.text: Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If PW-3 was confronted with her previous statement, she could have offered her explanation whether her brother had indeed suffered injuries in the fight or not.
Hence this court is not in a position to appreciate her evidence, in the light of there being no confrontation with her previous statement by the counsel for revisionist.
Further, even there is no MLC on record of brother of PW-3 and even PW-3 never deposed on oath regarding her brother suffering any kind of injuries in the fight.

Even PW-8 SI Ajeet, who is Investigating Officer of this case, had categorically deposed that there were only two male injured, who had sustained injuries in this case i.e. PW-1 and PW-2 and the counsel for accused had not doubted the said version of the IO as no suggestion was given that even PW-3 Pooja's brother had also sustained injuries in the fight.
Therefore, there is no material on record to show that prosecution had intentionally withheld about the injuries being suffered by the brother of PW-3 Ms Pooja in the fight.
31.Further

, although it is true that in the statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C of PW-4 Ms Kiran Gupta, there is reference regarding video recording but PW-4 never deposed on oath in her evidence regarding the said video recording.

The counsel for the revisionist did not confront PW-4 with her previous statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C, wherein there is a mention about video recording and, therefore, Ld.
Counsel for revisionist can not take the benefit of its non- Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 15/17 production during the trial.

sentences.text: even it is assumed that video recording was prepared of the incident by PW-4 then also no reason have been put forth by the revisionist as to why he made no application during the course of trial for its production.
Therefore, non-production of video recording is not fatal to the prosecution case.

33.The contention of ld. Counsel for revisionist that injuries were caused on the person of PW-2 by accused Surjeet Singh @ Dr. Sidhu as per the evidence of Pw-1 and revisionist has been wrongly convicted for being present at the spot deserves to be rejected.

The reason for the same is that both PW-1 and PW-2 have deposed that the revisionist and the other accused persons including accused Surjeet Singh @ Dr. Sidhu had got into a fight with them and during the course of fight accused Surjeet Singh @ Dr. Sidhu had caused injuries on the person of Pw-2 with the use of danda.

Therefore, the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 establishes on record that injuries on the person of PW-2 was caused by accused Surjeet Singh @ Dr. Sidhu pursuant to the common intention of all accused persons.
Therefore, revisionist was rightly convicted for the offence U/s 323/34 IPC.
34.In the light of aforementioned discussion

, the evidence which had come on record before the trial court was to the effect that PW-1 was contesting elections for Delhi Vidhan Sabha, 2020 and during the course of campaigning alongwith his party workers in the Sangam Vihar area, he Crl Rev No.
58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 16/17 alongwith his party workers were attacked by the revisionist and other accused persons pursuant to common intention with a view to prevent PW-1 and PW-2 and his party workers from campaigning in their area.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Ld. Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 8/17 Trial court has based its findings of conviction upon the testimony of prosecution witnesses i.e. PW-1 to PW-6.
Shivbhawan Ojha had specifically named the revisionist as one of the assailants in his examination-in- chief.
Therefore the identity of the revisionist was established beyond doubt.
Since PW-2 Sh. Shivbhawan Ojha was injured himself, therefore, his testimony has got greater evidentiary value and it can not be believed that the injured witness would allow real culprit to escape and Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 12/17 would falsely implicate the accused persons.
The presence of injured/eye witness at the time and place of occurrence can not be doubted unless there are material contradictions in his deposition.
In the present case, nothing was brought out in the cross- examination of PW-2 to show that the testimony of PW -2 is not reliable or trustworthy.
On the contrary, the testimony of PW-2, that an altercation taken place during the course of election campaigning between the party workers and his brother PW-1 and the opposite party of the revisionist in the Sangam Vihar area is duly corroborated by other persons of the campaigning party i.e. PW-3 to PW-6.
Ld. trial court had rightly relied upon the settled law that the testimony of witnesses, who have turned hostile and were cross-examined by prosecution can not be rejected in toto and the same is admissible to the extent their version is found to be corroborated by other reliable evidence.
In the present case, Ld.Trial Court had only relied upon the version of PW-3 to PW-6 regarding the fight which took place during the course of election campaigning which was duly corroborated by the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and I do not find any illegality in the same.
The reason for the same is that the statement of witnesses recorded U/s 161 Cr.P.C is in the nature of previous statement and they can only be used for the purpose of contradiction as per Section 162 Cr.P.C.
In the present case, during the evidence of PW-3 Pooja, the said witness was never confronted with her previous statement recorded U/s 161 Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 14/17 Cr.P.C with regard to her brother suffering injuries on his head during the course of fight.
If PW-3 was confronted with her previous statement, she could have offered her explanation whether her brother had indeed suffered injuries in the fight or not.
Hence this court is not in a position to appreciate her evidence, in the light of there being no confrontation with her previous statement by the counsel for revisionist.
Further, even there is no MLC on record of brother of PW-3 and even PW-3 never deposed on oath regarding her brother suffering any kind of injuries in the fight.
The counsel for the revisionist did not confront PW-4 with her previous statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C, wherein there is a mention about video recording and, therefore, Ld.
Counsel for revisionist can not take the benefit of its non- Crl Rev No. 58/2023 Dinesh Mohaniya Vs. State of Delhi 15/17 production during the trial.

Therefore, non-production of video recording is not fatal to the prosecution case.
Therefore, revisionist was rightly convicted for the offence U/s 323/34 IPC.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, Ld. Trial court had rightly convicted the revisionist for the offence U/s 323/34 IPC and I do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment or in the impugned sentence order.
Accordingly, revision petition is dismissed.
